services.name: openthread-border-router
entrypoint:
set -uo pipefail
SETTINGS=/data/settings.env
load_settings() {
  CONFIGURED=0; DEVICE=""; BAUDRATE=""; FLOW_CONTROL=""; BACKBONE_IF=""
  FIREWALL=""; NAT64=""; AUTOFLASH_FIRMWARE=""
  [ -f "$$SETTINGS" ] || return
  while IFS='=' read -r key val; do
    case "$$key" in
      DEVICE|BAUDRATE|FLOW_CONTROL|BACKBONE_IF|FIREWALL|NAT64|AUTOFLASH_FIRMWARE|CONFIGURED)
        export "$$key=$$val" ;;
    esac
  done < "$$SETTINGS"
}
echo "[otbr] waiting for first-run setup to complete (open the app to configure)..."
while true; do
  load_settings
  if [ "$${CONFIGURED:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -n "$${DEVICE:-}" ] && [ -e "$${DEVICE:-/nonexistent}" ]; then
    break
  fi
  echo "[otbr] not configured yet — retrying in 5s"
  sleep 5
done
echo "[otbr] configured (DEVICE=$$DEVICE BACKBONE_IF=$${BACKBONE_IF:-}) — starting border router"
# Record the settings we are launching with so the wizard can tell when
# the live border router matches the saved config (vs. a pending restart).
cat "$$SETTINGS" > /data/.applied 2>/dev/null || true
find / -type f -name app.js -path '*frontend/res/js/*' 2>/dev/null \
  | xargs -r sed -i "s/restServerPort = '8081'/restServerPort = '$${OTBR_REST_PORT:-8081}'/"
# s6-overlay must run as PID 1, so exec it. A background watcher restarts
# the container when settings change: it asks s6 to shut down with a
# non-zero exit code (via s6's container-results file), which restart:
# on-failure then brings back up to re-read the new settings. A normal
# Umbrel stop exits 0, so it is not restarted.
(
  ref="$$(cat "$$SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null)"
  while sleep 5; do
    if [ "$$(cat "$$SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null)" != "$$ref" ]; then
      echo "[otbr] settings changed — restarting to apply"
      echo 1 > /run/s6-linux-init-container-results/exitcode 2>/dev/null || true
      kill -TERM 1 2>/dev/null || true
      exit 0
    fi
  done
) &
exec /init
